names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουλίου, «Οσία Άννα η εν τω Λευκαδίω», with the rank word and the byname left off. The page gives the place in two forms, «η εν τω Λευκαδίω (ή Λευκάτη)».

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Η Οσία Άννα η εν τω Λευκαδίω (ή Λευκάτη) έζησε στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Θεοφίλου του εικονομάχου (829 - 842 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign, which is the only one the page prints with years, and it marks when she was living and not when she died: the same page has her fifty years a nun afterwards. The page then says her suitor asked for her «με την συγκατάθεση του βασιλιά Βασιλείου», with the consent of the emperor Basil, who reigned long after Theophilus; that disagreement is the page's own and no year is drawn from it.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Ιουλίου — «Οσία Άννα η εν τω Λευκαδίω»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page dates her twice and the two do not agree: the reign of Theophilus the iconoclast, which it gives as 829–842, and then the consent of «ο βασιλιάς Βασίλειος» to her suitor's request. The reign with years is taken into `dates` and the other is recorded here; nothing is reconciled. The corpus holds a dozen women named Anna and none of them hers — Anna of Adrianople, of Larissa, of Novgorod, the Princess, the mother of Samuel, the two bare martyr entries and the twentieth-century Russians are all other women. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn.
